skill.name: pdf
skill.description: PDF processing toolkit for extracting text and tables, creating and editing PDFs, merging and splitting documents, rendering pages, and filling PDF forms.
skill.summary: Process, analyze, create, and fill PDF documents with guided Python and command-line workflows.
skill.author: Azeem-2

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, JavaScript template literals, Python f-strings, comments, and expected local PDF file operations. No prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, or hidden network behavior was found in the cited files. The main operational concern is safe handling of local input and output files during PDF workflows.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts accept caller-provided output paths.
remediation.suggestion: Validate output paths or document that outputs should stay inside a dedicated working directory.

remediation.issue: Command-line examples can alter, decrypt, or overwrite PDFs.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to run commands only on copies and confirm destructive operations before execution.

remediation.issue: External dependencies are assumed by the workflows.
remediation.suggestion: List required packages and command-line tools with safe installation guidance.

content.value_statement: PDF workflows often require extraction, form filling, and file conversion across several tools. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured steps and scripts for common PDF tasks.
actual_capabilities: Extract text and tables from PDFs with pypdf, pdfplumber, and related examples.
Merge, split, rotate, crop, encrypt, watermark, and repair PDF files.
Render PDF pages to images for visual review or OCR workflows.
Create new PDFs and reports with ReportLab examples.
Identify and fill PDF form fields using included helper scripts.
Use command-line examples for qpdf, poppler-utils, pdftk, and pdfimages.
limitations: External libraries and command-line tools must be installed before related workflows run.
Scanned PDFs need OCR tools before text extraction is reliable.
Form filling can require visual checks because field locations vary by PDF.
Scripts write local output files and should run in a dedicated working directory.

use_cases.title: Fill Client Forms
use_cases.description: Prepare filled PDF forms from supplied user data while checking field IDs and visual placement.

use_cases.title: Extract Document Data
use_cases.description: Pull text, tables, and metadata from PDF packets for review, analysis, or spreadsheet preparation.

use_cases.title: Assemble PDF Deliverables
use_cases.description: Merge, split, watermark, rotate, or encrypt PDFs before sharing polished document packages.

prompt_templates.title: Extract PDF Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PDF skill to extract text from [file name]. Summarize each page and note tables that need separate extraction.

prompt_templates.title: Merge and Split Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PDF skill to merge these PDFs in order: [files]. Then split pages [range] into a separate output file.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a PDF Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PDF skill to inspect [form.pdf], identify fillable fields, prepare field values from this data, and create a filled copy.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PDF skill to process every PDF in [folder], extract tables, save reviewed outputs, and report files that fail.

output_examples.input: Extract tables from a quarterly invoice packet.
output: A page-by-page summary of detected tables.
Notes about pages that need manual review.

output_examples.input: Fill a benefit enrollment PDF from approved user details.
output: A filled PDF copy saved under a new filename.
A short validation summary of matched form fields.
A warning for any field that could not be located.

output_examples.input: Merge several signed documents into one delivery packet.
output_examples.output: A combined PDF with the requested order, plus a brief list of included source files.

best_practices: Work on copies of original PDFs before merging, repairing, decrypting, or filling forms.
Use explicit input and output filenames in a dedicated project directory.
Validate form field IDs, bounding boxes, and rendered previews before delivering final PDFs.
anti_patterns: Do not run commands on untrusted PDFs without isolating outputs and reviewing generated files.
Do not overwrite originals unless the user explicitly requests that action.
Do not assume scanned documents contain selectable text; verify OCR needs first.

faq.question: Can this skill create new PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes ReportLab examples for creating reports and pdf-lib examples for JavaScript PDF generation.

faq.question: Can it fill PDF forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports fillable fields and annotation-based workflows for non-fillable forms.

faq.question: Does it upload PDFs to a network service?
faq.answer: No upload behavior was found. The included URLs are documentation references in comments.

faq.question: What dependencies are needed?
faq.answer: Workflows may need pypdf, pdfplumber, ReportLab, pdf2image, poppler-utils, qpdf, pdftk, or OCR tools.

faq.question: Can it process scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes, but scanned PDFs need OCR tools such as pytesseract after page images are generated.

faq.question: How should users avoid file mistakes?
faq.answer: Use copies of source PDFs, choose explicit output names, and run scripts in a dedicated folder.
